Constructed my own genuine-selection candidate (min_edge 0.15->0.24): combined_score=2.4384568716289445 strictly beats baseline (1.2628...), worst_window_oos_net_usd=4.526752095788865 >= 0.

Grid-searched the full (min_edge, min_confidence) threshold space (~1350 combos) for a degenerate/near-zero-variance candidate that could inflate the ratio: zero beat-baseline candidates found with std_oos_net_usd < 0.05 — the metric is not gameable via naive threshold search on this fixture. The single most over-fit candidate found (score=4.30, ~3.4x baseline) is caught by the REQ-RH2 tripwire (>3x population_best) before it could even become eligible_for_adversary_review, let alone auto-promote.

dimensions.name: PROMOTE_GATE_INTEGRITY
findings: (a) ORDER: assess_candidate() in lib/promote_gate.py runs scope_guard -> evaluate() cascade (stage1+stage2) -> tripwire_check, all before promote_gate_run.py ever reaches its adversary subprocess call (guarded by `if not assessment['eligible_for_adversary_review']: ... return` at promote_gate_run.py:208-214, BEFORE the `_invoke_adversary` call at line 216+). Live-verified: ran promote_gate_run.py --dry-run against a hand-crafted regressing candidate (min_edge 0.10/min_confidence 0.0) -> logged 'NOT ELIGIBLE for adversary review (no LLM call made)', zero subprocess spawned, verdict.json adversary_invoked=false.

(b) REAL ADVERSARY: promote_gate_run.py._invoke_adversary spawns `claude --model opus --dangerously-skip-permissions --print --output-format json --json-schema ... --add-dir <repo_root>` via subprocess.run with the prompt on stdin — not a stub. Independently authenticated evidence/close-loop/handcrafted_candidate_adversary_verdict.json's adversary_session_id (8593a18a-4186-4c7b-83cc-ac866f69eda4) by locating and reading the REAL local Claude Code session transcript at ~/.claude/projects/-Users-anicca-anicca--worktrees-self-improve-close-loop/8593a18a-....jsonl: model field = claude-opus-4-8 (Opus), first user message byte-matches _build_prompt()'s template, and the assistant's own transcript text ('I'll spot-check the actual strategy file to verify the mechanism of min_edge... Confirmed... at line 63') shows the adversary genuinely used a tool to independently verify the diff before rendering its PASS verdict — this cannot be fabricated after the fact from inside promote_gate_run.py; it is proof of a real, independent Opus process.

(c) DRY-RUN SAFETY: promote_gate_run.py's `if dry_run: <synthetic report, no call> else: promote_gate.promote_if_approved(...)` branch is UNCONDITIONAL on the decision outcome — dry-run can never reach promote_if_approved/promote.promote regardless of whether the adversary said PASS or FAIL (fixes the documented prior bug where promote(commit=False) still wrote the file). Live-verified: ran promote_gate_run.py --dry-run against an ineligible candidate; strategy-file md5 identical before/after, `git status --short` on the file empty. No dedicated automated pytest unit test exercises promote_gate_run.py's own main()/dry-run path specifically (it is deliberately excluded from the fast pytest suite per the module's own docstring, since an eligible-path dry-run still makes a real paid adversary call) — this is a minor coverage gap, not a functional hole, since the guarding code path is a trivial, statically-verifiable unconditional if/else and was live-exercised above.

(d) COMMIT GATE: gate_math.stage_gate/decide_promotion requires stage1_pass AND stage2_pass(beats_baseline) AND tripwire_clear AND adversary_verdict=="PASS" (exact string) before decision['promote']=True; promote_if_approved only calls lib.promote.promote when decision['promote'] is True. Confirmed via tests/test_adversary_disapprove.py (all 5 tests pass): FAIL verdict, missing/erroring verdict, and ineligible-candidate cases all assert promote.promote is NEVER called (mocked and asserted not-called); PASS-on-eligible case asserts it IS called exactly once.

git log across both the worktree and main repo shows no 'feat(self-improve): promote candidate ...' commit ever landed — consistent with the documented fact that nothing has actually been promoted yet.

summary: PASS on all 7 dimensions after independent re-verification (not trusting any evidence file at face value). Re-ran ledger_reader.py against the real earn-ledger.jsonl and cross-checked it against a from-scratch call into the actual ledger.mjs (JS): both agree exactly on realized_net_usd=8.4731, profitable_row_count=6, total_rows=30. Independently constructed leverage-only and genuine-selection candidates and confirmed risk_adjusted_score is exactly leverage-invariant (bit-identical combined_score) while genuinely rewarding selection changes; grid-searched the full threshold space and found no way to game a near-zero-variance score past the tripwire/cap. Authenticated the handcrafted candidate's adversary verdict by locating and reading the actual local Claude Code session transcript for its claimed session_id — confirmed a real claude-opus-4-8 process that used a tool to independently verify the diff, not a fabricated verdict. Live-exercised the --dry-run path against both an eligible and an ineligible candidate and confirmed zero file writes / zero unnecessary LLM calls. Ran the full pytest suite (44/44 green) and spot-broke two different modules to confirm the tests are non-vacuous, then fully reverted (confirmed byte-identical via diff, clean git status). Confirmed the documentation is honest about the synthetic-fixture limitation and about no openevolve-discovered candidate having cleared the new risk-adjusted gate yet. No blocking findings. One non-blocking observation: promote_gate_run.py's dry-run no-write guarantee has no dedicated automated pytest test (only live-exercised in this review + a trivially-inspectable unconditional if/else) — recommend adding one, but it is not a functional hole. Another non-blocking observation: the launchd plist is not currently loaded and still points at the main repo's pre-close-loop script, which is expected pre-merge state, not a defect in this branch's code.
